A packs Right-side outputs in reversed order (copying scan-order outputs left-to-right into the tail), while B places each output at its correct destination-edge index.

A strips trailing zeros from a big-endian digit vector so any number ending in 0 (e.g. "10") parses to the wrong value, whereas C is canonical little-endian throughout with correct parse precedence, formatting, grouping and arithmetic.
C validates the port before the host (wrong precedence, e.g. "x://:" gives InvalidPort instead of InvalidHost), while A follows the required order and correct offsets for all components.

B detects empty segments during splitting before validating earlier segments left to right and C fails to strip the slash on removal redirects and can redirect root, while A validates left to right and handles redirects and root correctly.

Only C validates segments strictly left to right (captures, wildcard position and escapes in one pass) before the trailing-slash check, whereas A checks statics before captures, B finds empty segments and wildcard position out of order, and D reports the trailing slash before segment errors (fails /%GG/ -> 1).

A's tie-break uses the empty range (3..=0) so it never prefers the lexicographically greatest change, and B reports TubeLimit in escrow insertion order rather than ascending denomination order, while C handles greedy, exhaustive tie-breaking and ascending TubeLimit correctly.

B reports Escape at the first textual ".." occurrence rather than at the offending parent component, while A tracks exact component offsets (including the tilde prefix) and otherwise matches all normalize/resolve rules.

Only C checks the full item structure (both endpoints, starred endpoints, and digit-only step) for InvalidSyntax at item start before any numeric validation, whereas A reports end-endpoint and step syntax errors at the wrong offset and after numeric checks, and B validates the step syntax only after numeric checks.
